regime.label: +302.7 total net GEX is the first positive reading in 11 sessions and the cumulative curve finally crosses zero at 1,150, but with 75 days left, +749 contracts of OI added today and a -4,746.4 trough still parked at 1,040, this is an insurance book thickening above spot, not a pin
evidence: +1,150.0 of net dealer GEX now sits within 20 points of the money (1,040-1,070), up from +985.4 on 10-13 and +336.0 five sessions ago on 10-08. The per-strike hinge is 1,050 (+626.4) against 1,040 (-225.8), so spot at 1,054.9 stands 4.9 points inside the stabilising side of the chain.

+302.7 is total net GEX across 960-1,150, the first positive total since 2026-09-29 (+374.5) and a +916.0 swing from -613.3 yesterday. The cumulative sum crosses zero at 1,150 - the first gamma flip present in the chain since 09-29 - but that is 95.1 points above spot, so the whole traded corridor still sits beneath the structural flip while dampening locally at 1,050-1,100.

+749 contracts of open interest were added in one session (17,534 to 18,283) and +2,000 in five (+12.3%), call OI +408 against put OI +341. +355 of the call build landed at 1,060-1,090 on 615 of the day's 875 call contracts with the 1,080 call bid +0.30 vol - volume, OI and IV all confirming live upside flow by the Vol2Vol test.

11.61% ATM IV prices a 7.71-point 1-sigma day (0.73%) and has drifted +0.22 points higher over five sessions (11.39% on 10-08), so nothing is compressing further. The 1,847-contract 960 put wall grew +56 on 93 contracts of volume but sits 94.9 points (9.0%) below spot - structural insurance, not an active level.

S50Z26.today_summary: 1,054.9 closes +4.5 points higher and 4.9 points above its own 1,050 max-pain strike, the seventh straight session inside a 1,045.3-1,054.9 band and the seventh with max pain frozen at 1,050. 875 call contracts traded against 938 puts for a 1.07 P/C volume ratio, but the distribution matters more than the ratio: 615 of the call contracts hit 1,060-1,090 and lifted call OI there +355, while 685 of the put contracts clustered at 1,000-1,050 at or below spot. 1.0023 P/C OI on 18,283 total contracts says standing positioning is dead balanced, with the long-gamma shelf at 1,050-1,100 now worth +3,055.4 of GEX against a -4,746.4 cumulative trough at 1,040. 11.61% ATM IV and a 7.71-point 1-sigma day keep the implied corridor at 1,047.2-1,062.6 for tomorrow, inside the 25-delta band of 1,010-1,080.
what_changed: Total net GEX flipped sign +916.0 to +302.7, the first positive total in 11 sessions, as the 1,060 strike added +84 call OI (+458.2 GEX) and 1,080 added +158 (+844.9). A gamma flip reappeared in the chain at 1,150 for the first time since 09-29.

Call OI rose +408 against +341 puts, reversing yesterday's put-led build (+59 calls against +183 puts); +355 of it at 1,060-1,090 on 615 contracts of volume, with call volume itself +420 (455 to 875).

The near-money put wall migrated 1,000 to 1,040 (823 OI) as spot at 1,054.9 pushed the 1,033-contract 1,000 strike 54.9 points away, outside the +/-5% band - a band shift, not an unwind; 1,000 put OI still grew +54 on 135 contracts.
25-delta skew widened -1.28 to -2.06, but the 25-delta put band stepped 1,000 to 1,010 (IV 12.45% to 11.29%); on fixed strikes the 1,000 put against the 1,080 call moved only -0.78 to -0.90.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: The window's defining move is the long-gamma shelf above spot thickening +40.7% in five sessions: 1,050/1,060/1,080/1,100 carried +2,171.0 of GEX on 10-08 and carry +3,055.4 now, which dragged the chain total from -326.6 to +302.7 and restored a gamma flip at 1,150. Max pain has not moved since 10-06 (1,050 for seven sessions, 1,060 before that) and spot has closed in a 9.6-point band of 1,045.3-1,054.9 across the whole stretch, which is the shelf doing its work rather than expiry mechanics - there are still 75 days left. Both walls are frozen for all 21 sessions on file: 1,100 calls (1,345 OI, +56 in five sessions) and 960 puts (1,847 OI, +155). What has not improved is the asymmetry below: the cumulative trough has sat at the 1,040 strike for 10 straight sessions and only shallowed +178.3 to -4,746.4, so dealers still dampen at 1,050-1,100 and chase under 1,040. IV refuses to compress - 11.39% to 11.61% over the five sessions, +0.22 points - so the premium case rests on the frozen 1,050 anchor and a 7.71-point 1-sigma, not on a vol collapse.

strategies.name: Iron condor 1010P / 990P x 1100C / 1120C
strategies.rationale: Sells the two boundaries the chain actually defends - the 1,010 25-delta put (439 OI) and the 1,345-contract 1,100 call wall where dealers hold +1,125.9 of long gamma - against a +1,150.0 near-money gamma shelf, a 1,050 pain strike frozen for eight sessions and a 9.6-point realised range.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point wing width minus net credit, per side (20 points = 4,000 baht at 200 baht per point). Only one wing can finish in the money.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close below 1,040, where cumulative net GEX bottoms at -4,746.4 and dealer hedging switches from fading to chasing, or above the 1,100 call wall.

strategies.name: Put credit spread 1010 / 990
strategies.rationale: The same pin thesis as the condor with the call wing dropped, because 615 of today's 875 call contracts and +355 of call OI landed at 1,060-1,090 with the 1,080 call bid +0.30 vol - live upside flow by the Vol2Vol test is the wrong thing to be short of, while 1,010 sits 44.9 points below a spot that has not closed under 1,045.3 in seven sessions.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width minus net credit = 4,000 baht minus credit received.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close below 1,040 (the -4,746.4 GEX trough), which puts the short 1,010 strike inside one 7.71-point sigma of being tested.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1040 / 1010
strategies.rationale: Buys the amplification shelf directly: every strike from 1,040 down to 960 carries negative net GEX, the 1,040 put is the cheapest vol in the band at 9.57% (against 11.29% at 1,010 and 14.89% at 960), and 122 contracts traded there today - defined-risk insurance against the one structure that would chase a break lower.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = the net debit paid; maximum value 30 points (6,000 baht) if settlement is at or below 1,010.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1,060, where the +458.2 of GEX at that strike plus the 1,100 wall keep dealers fading rallies and the hedge decays against 75 days of theta.

S50Z26.prediction: 11.61% ATM IV and +1,150.0 of near-money dealer gamma argue for another session inside 1,047.2-1,062.6, with the 1,050 pain strike and the +626.4 of GEX on it the centre of gravity for an eighth session. The directional tilt is marginally higher - +355 of fresh call OI at 1,060-1,090 against a 1.0023 P/C OI that has stopped rising - so the balance of flow favours the 1,060-1,080 band over a retest of 1,045. A daily close below 1,040 invalidates all of it: that is where cumulative net GEX bottoms at -4,746.4 and dealer hedging turns from fading moves to chasing them, with 980-1,000 (1,729 combined put OI) the next shelf.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no instruction to execute anything. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind pinning are structurally weaker than for share-settled single stocks: treat the 1,050 max-pain anchor as a tendency, not a guarantee, especially with 75 days to the 2026-12-29 last trading date. Defined risk is not risk-free - the capped loss on every structure above is real and does occur. Open interest is a burden map, not a directional signal: it does not reveal who is long or short, hedge or speculation, and a macro or liquidity shock can overrun the option structure outright.
